name: Calamine

lead: Calamine is a topical lotion or cream made from powdered zinc oxide with a small amount of ferric oxide, which gives it its pink colour. It is a long-established over-the-counter skin soother used for mild itching, insect bites, sunburn and weeping skin from plant rashes.

For appearance, people use it to calm irritated, red or oozing skin and to dry out blemishes, and it has been used for acne and acne scars. Evidence specific to cosmetic use is limited, while its general soothing role is well known.

paras: It is shaken, dabbed or spread onto the affected area as a thin layer and left to dry, then washed off. Spot use on individual blemishes is common among those who use it for acne. It is usually used for short periods on irritated skin.

Skin irritation is the main listed side effect, and it may damage the barrier of sensitive skin. Wikipedia notes dermatologist warnings against using it as a makeup primer. It is considered safe during pregnancy and should not be used on large areas, deep wounds or near the eyes without advice.

angle.text: Calamine dries and soothes irritated skin, which can reduce the redness and discomfort that make skin look inflamed. Some people spot-apply it on blemishes.

lead: Calamine is a topical medication made from zinc oxide with about 0.5 percent ferric oxide, giving it a pink tint, and is typically sold as a lotion [1]. Modern versions can also contain phenol and calcium hydroxide [1]. It is used for mild itching, sunburn, insect bites, allergic irritation and other mild skin conditions, and it may help dry out weeping skin [1].

Wikipedia says the lotion has been used since about 1500 BC and that its name comes from calamine, an older name for the zinc ores smithsonite and hemimorphite [1]. Grokipedia, an AI-generated source, describes calamine as a skin protectant that forms a barrier and has a cooling, astringent effect, and lists use for poison ivy, insect bites, sunburn and chickenpox [2].

For appearance, calamine is used on irritated or inflamed skin and on blemishes. Wikipedia notes its use for acne and acne scars, while warning that it may damage the barrier of sensitive skin and citing dermatologist warnings against use as a makeup primer [1].
infobox: Zinc oxide with about 0.5% ferric oxide [1]
Itch, sunburn, insect bites, weeping skin [1]

paras: Calamine is used for mild itching and conditions like sunburn, insect bites and allergic irritation and may help dry weeping skin [1]. The FDA recommends it for weeping from poison ivy, oak and sumac while noting that cold compresses and topical corticosteroids can help with pain and itch [1]. A dermatology review lists calamine among zinc preparations used as photoprotecting and soothing agents [3].
Cosmetic uses reported include acne and acne scars, although it may damage the barrier of sensitive skin [1].

Skin irritation is the main side effect [1]. Grokipedia advises avoiding large areas, deep wounds and use near the eyes without medical advice [2]. Wikipedia says dermatologists have warned against using it as a makeup primer [1].

Wikipedia states that the lotion has been used since about 1500 BC and that calamine was once the name for zinc ores [1]. A 1968 pharmacy journal article described preparing calamine lotion with microcrystalline cellulose [4].

Studies on calamine are mostly about medical itch. A Cochrane review of pityriasis rosea interventions covers a scaly, itchy rash lasting 2 to 12 weeks [5]. A review asked whether calamine or antihistamines relieve itch in children with chickenpox [6]. A study looked at calamine lotion for skin irritation in children in casts [7]. No studies of calamine for acne or appearance are cited here.
